answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Ledger. Each identity must periodically answer a challenge derived from its own onyx interaction history, and answers are sealed as a cipher under a key the agent alone holds. Clones sharing one source produce identical histories, so they cannot diverge; the ledger detects correlated responses and voids the duplicated identities at once, a mesa of revoked slots. An attacker pays full compute and storage per clone to synthesize distinct histories, plus forfeited work when correlation surfaces.
